summary: The round-one theorem framing, quantifiers, import boundaries and stated formal-assurance limits are coherent. I found no framing defect requiring revision. This is a continue decision: I have not yet audited all family-to-model implications, finite leaves or arbitrary-support reductions, so this round does not certify the complete theorem.

findings.statement: H27 and Jin are imported mathematical theorems; local scope inspection and selected prior replays do not constitute independent reproduction of their proofs. The manuscript expressly preserves this distinction.
findings.disposition: Retain the source and assurance qualifications in sections 2 and 7. No additional assumption is inferred solely from the absence of a local end-to-end formalization.

findings.statement: The five R15 Lean roots prove natural-number inequality interfaces with geometric premises supplied as hypotheses; they do not prove Theorem 2 or Theorem 1. The manuscript accurately limits their scope.
findings.disposition: Later review must separately inspect the ordinary derivations supplying those premises and the finite predicates. No compiler run or axiom audit was independently repeated in this round.

checks.method: Computed SHA256 of manuscript bytes and canonical compact sorted-key JSON for snapshot, contract and roster; compared six inspected evidence-file hashes with the snapshot.
checks.observation: The supplied manuscript and canonical snapshot hashes match exactly. Canonical contract and roster commitments match. global-proof, global-dag, external-scope, prior-unlock, direct-jin and formal-scalar file hashes all match their entries.

checks.method: Inspected manuscript sections 1, 3 and 4 and GLOBAL67-ordinary-theorem.md, Literal statement and Mathematical proof by maximum degree.
checks.observation: The theorem concerns finite simple exactly four-uniform families on arbitrary ground sets, with three distinct members and empty cores forbidden. Excluding exactly 68 members implies the at-least-68 statement by arbitrary hereditary restriction; the text recomputes degree facts on the fixed restricted family. M is explicitly the maximum-size parameter, so the claimed upper bound is 67.

checks.scope: H27 transfer to neighbourhood and graph bounds
checks.method: Checked the implication directly against the definitions in manuscript section 3 and EXTERNAL-H27-JIN-SCOPE.md, Application to the current conventions.
checks.observation: For an actual R, any two disjoint members of its disjoint class would form an empty-core sunflower with R. The class is therefore an intersecting SF4 family and H27 yields the closed-meeting bound 68-27=41. Independent sets of the disjointness graph are intersecting subfamilies, and graph triangles are prohibited empty-core sunflowers.

checks.scope: High-level dependency direction and guarded imports
checks.method: Inspected GLOBAL67-dependency-roadmap.md sections 1-2 and PRIOR_DELTA18_UNLOCK.md alongside manuscript sections 3-4.
checks.observation: The displayed proof order is cap20, D20, D19, activation of the cap18 package, D18, D17, D16, cap15. The prior global upper68 is explicitly excluded as a premise; cross-star, crowding, minimum7 and R61 are introduced only after their cap18 and mu41 guards. This checks the stated dependency contract, not every transitive code-level dependency.

checks.method: Inspected manuscript sections 3.1-3.2 and the complete-link scope in GLOBAL67-dependency-roadmap.md section 2.
checks.observation: The manuscript explicitly retains arbitrary exterior multiplicities for proper traces, reserves binarity for full four-point traces, and distinguishes an actual complete link from a guessed sublink. It states the required actual-family-to-feasible-point implication in the correct direction and does not infer it from a certificate. Detailed model-row verification remains for later rounds.

checks.scope: Direct Jin A3 transfer without assuming an occupied image
checks.method: Read LOW15-direct-Jin-A3-addon.md and checked the cyclic identity coefficientwise for all eight indices using a bounded standard-library script; checked the integer strict-threshold inequality.
checks.observation: The script verified b_i+b_(i+3)+b_(i+5)=sum(a)+a_i for every index and 25*11>4*68. Neighbourhood preimages are independent even for empty fibres, giving b_i<=27 first; sum(e)=12 then gives a_i>=1, after which b_i>=25 follows from an actual vertex. The proof uses only homomorphism implications.
